title: Risk-based schedule for tenant audit readiness with staggered deliverables
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Create a risk-prioritized rollout schedule and communications plan to bring tenant cohorts to SOC2/ISO readiness. Deliverables are staggered so high-risk tenants follow a fast lane with additional controls while lower-risk tenants use a self-service checklist. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, Design, Security, and Customer Success for sequencing, blackout windows, and evidence handoff.
milestones: M1: Cohort definition and risk rubric finalized - 2025-07-10
M2: Core audit controls implemented for high-risk cohort (SSO, audit-log retention) - 2025-08-01
M3: Simulation run for high-risk cohort (dry-run tenant onboarding) - 2025-08-15
M4: Evidence collection template and automation hooks ready - 2025-08-25
M5: Low/medium cohort onboarding self-service release - 2025-09-05
M6: Final compliance readiness signoff and customer communication - 2025-09-15
updates: 2025-07-01: Kickoff meeting — aligned on three tenant cohorts (high, medium, low) and decision to prioritize high-risk tenants for initial controls.
2025-07-08: Security review meeting — agreed on audit-log retention baseline (90 days) and SSO SAML baseline configuration; Security requested HLD doc for SSO fallback (link in links).
2025-07-14: Eng provided ETA for audit-log indexing pipeline (ENG-2841) — scoped as minimal viable indexing with retention tag; assigned spike to ENG team for performance impact measurements.
2025-07-28: Design review — onboarding checklist UX accepted with action items: add evidence upload flow and per-tenant progress bar (see Drive mockups).
2025-08-04: Dry-run scheduled for two internal tenants; found missing telemetry for session-init events — follow-up ENG task created (ENG-3910).
2025-08-10: Legal signoff pending on data transfer text; Customer Success drafted targeted comms for cohort A customers.
tradeoffs: Speed vs completeness: rolling a minimal audit-log pipeline for high-risk tenants now reduces time-to-compliance but requires a follow-up to expand retention and indexing for analytics.

Automation vs manual evidence: automating evidence extraction increases engineer work up-front but reduces customer friction later; decided to automate core controls and keep optional manual steps for niche evidence.
Single-cutover vs staggered windows: staggered windows reduce blast radius for regressions but increase coordination overhead across teams.
acceptance_criteria: All high-risk cohort tenants onboarded using the new checklist and SSO configuration without manual intervention (>90%).
Audit-log retention enforced and accessible via compliance dashboard for onboarded tenants.
Evidence export for auditors generated from automation hooks and validated by Security team.
Customer Success has templated communications and rollback plan in place.
risks: Indexing audit-logs may increase infra cost by ~12% for high-volume tenants; contingency budget needed.
SSO SAML edge-cases across older IdPs may require manual customer engineering support during first wave.
Evidence automation could surface false positives; Security will need to sign off on heuristics.
next_steps: Complete ENG spike for audit-log performance (due 2025-07-20) and determine if additional batching is required.
Run scheduled simulation with two internal tenants on 2025-08-15 and capture telemetry for post-mortem.
Finalize customer comms templates and CS runbook by 2025-08-20.
Prep post-onboarding support rota and on-call handoff notes with Support and SRE.
